question: How do structural modifications of gold surfaces influence the band structure and alignment of seven-armchair graphene nanoribbons?
answer: Structural modifications of gold surfaces—specifically, step-edge reshaping and missing row reconstruction on the vicinal Au(16 14 15) surface—directly influence the band structure and alignment of seven-armchair graphene nanoribbons (7-AGNRs). The high-temperature growth process induces these substrate changes, lowering the dehalogenation temperature and enabling preferential alignment of 7-AGNRs along close-packed directions. This alignment facilitates angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements, revealing the occupied frontier band at the Γ point, with band maximum and effective mass values consistent with theoretical predictions. The reconstructed surface thus plays a critical role in defining the electronic properties of the nanoribbons.

### Task 1: Summarize the purpose of the paper
The paper investigates the synthesis and electronic properties of seven-armchair graphene nanoribbons (7-AGNRs) grown on a vicinal gold surface (Au(16 14 15)) through on-surface chemistry. The study focuses on understanding how the substrate's step-edge reshaping and reconstruction during the growth process influence the alignment and band structure of the nanoribbons. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), the authors identify and characterize the energy and effective mass of the occupied frontier band of 7-AGNRs, validating theoretical predictions.
